adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: calling `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` exists, but many RSS items only have `description`, causing a NoMethodError/nil dereference and crashing processing. The candidate additionally notes the lack of per-item rescue causing the loop to abort, but the core issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `post = embed.post` is nil once the post is deleted so `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` raises; revise!'s false return is discarded while `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` fires unconditionally, permanently marking the embed current and losing the update.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 — new top-level embed.css/embed.js assets reachable from no application manifest with no `config.assets.precompile` entry, so the whole feature raises "isn't precompiled" in production.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` never rescues HTTP errors/redirect loops/timeouts and topic_embed.rb never requires open-uri.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the `import_remote` method calls `open(url).read` but the file only `require`s `ruby-readability` (and `nokogiri` at top). There is no `require 'open-uri'` in this file, so `open` may not support HTTP URLs unless `open-uri` has been loaded elsewhere, making this a real potential runtime defect attributable to the diff. Also, `open(url)` can raise (timeouts, redirects, HTTP errors), and `import_remote` does not rescue those exceptions, so failures will bubble up and can crash the job/controller path that calls it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:25 — `TopicEmbed.create!` follows a non-atomic `exists?` check against a UNIQUE index with no `validates_uniqueness_of` and no rescue, so concurrent PollFeed + RetrieveTopic on the same URL raise unrescued RecordNotUnique.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a UNIQUE index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`) but `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic read-then-create: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then, if blank, `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :embed_url` and no rescue around `create!`. With concurrent callers (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` iterating items calling `TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` for the same URL), both can observe no row and then race to insert, causing an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` to be raised and not handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — `if post.present?` cannot distinguish success from failure because PostCreator#create returns the unsaved @post after ActiveRecord::Rollback, so a rolled-back creation runs `TopicEmbed.create!(topic_id: nil, post_id: nil)` into the NOT NULL constraint.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — documented as "Convert any relative URLs to absolute" but `href.start_with?('/')` misses document-relative URLs (`images/x.png`, `../post`) and corrupts protocol-relative `//cdn.example.com/x.png` into `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the code only rewrites links/images when the attribute `start_with?('/')`. This contradicts the comment “Convert any relative URLs to absolute” because document-relative URLs like `images/x.png` or `../post` are not rewritten at all. Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` also satisfy `start_with?('/')` and will be rewritten via `prefix + "/" + href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, producing `http(s)://<host>/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which is incorrect and effectively corrupts the URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — `topic_id_for_embed` does not exclude deleted topics and nothing declares `dependent: :destroy`, so deleting an embedded topic leaves a stale row that makes TopicView.new raise while perform_retrieve's `exists?` bail blocks re-import — the URL is permanently bricked.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces TopicEmbed rows keyed by embed_url and uses them as the sole guard for whether an embed has been retrieved. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) simply plucks `:topic_id` for a given URL without verifying the referenced topic still exists (or isn’t in a deleted state), and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` returns early if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), which only checks the embed row, not the topic. In `EmbedController#best`, a non-nil `topic_id` leads directly to `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with no rescue; if the topic has been destroyed/purged while the topic_embeds row remains, this can error and the retriever will never re-import because the stale embed row blocks retrieval. The diff also doesn’t show any association on Topic/Post with `dependent: :destroy` to prevent orphaned `topic_embeds` rows, so the orphan/stale-row scenario is possible with this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — `feed_key` builds a "feed-modified:" cache key read and written by nothing, leaving the If-Modified-Since / change-detection half of polling unimplemented dead code.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (building a `"feed-modified:"` SHA1-based key), but nothing in the diff calls `feed_key` or uses the resulting key to read/write any cache/redis value or HTTP conditional headers. The actual polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates items with no change-detection. So the finding that this is unused/dead code and that the change-detection half is unimplemented is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" stub only their own setting while `feed_polling_enabled` sits at its false default, so the && chain short-circuits and both tests pass identically if their guard clauses are deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples only stub their respective setting to nil, but do not stub `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Given the default in config/site_settings.yml is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, these specs will short-circuit on the first condition and never reach the URL/username checks, so they don't actually verify those guards (they would still pass if the URL/username conditions were removed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" passes because embeddable_host defaults to '' and ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess first, so `params.require(:embed_url)` and its status mapping are never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best`. `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. The diff sets the default `embeddable_host` to an empty string in `config/site_settings.yml`, so in the spec `get :best` (with no stubs) will fail in the before_filter before `params.require(:embed_url)` is evaluated. Therefore the example labeled "is 404 without an embed_url" can pass for the wrong reason (missing embeddable_host / referer check), and it does not actually exercise the missing-`embed_url` behavior or any status mapping for `params.require` failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic, TopicEmbed.import_remote, PollFeed#poll_feed and the layout postMessage resize handshake have zero test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in several places without corresponding specs. There is no spec file for the new regular job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is introduced in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` but `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only exercises `.import`, not `.import_remote`. For feed polling, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `execute` gating/dispatch, not the actual `poll_feed` logic (fetch/parse/import loop). The embed layout’s JS postMessage resize handshake in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` has no test coverage (and there are no JS/view specs added for it). So the finding that these specific items have zero test coverage is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — `comments.appendChild(iframe)` has no null guard so a host page missing #discourse-comments throws a TypeError; no README/admin docs for the required discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl globals or container element.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the embedding page does not contain an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be null and this will throw a TypeError at runtime. The additional claim about missing README/admin docs for required globals/container is not verifiable from this diff alone, but the null-guard issue is directly present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — exact string compare against a new free-text `embeddable_host` setting with no validator or www./apex normalization, so an admin entering `http://example.com` gets a bare 403 with no diagnostic; only one host is ever supportable.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer host is compared via `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. `URI(...).host` returns a bare hostname like `example.com`, while `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is a free-text string (`site_settings.yml` sets it as `''` with no shown validation/normalization). If an admin enters `http://example.com` (or includes `www.`), the comparison will fail and the controller raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` (likely a 403) even though the intent is correct. The setting also inherently supports only a single host string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` adds a per-thread network fetch with no rescue (one dead permalink aborts a multi-thousand-thread import) and silently drops the previously-passed `created_at`.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the import path was changed from creating the topic via `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (open-uri) and does not rescue network/HTTP errors, so a single dead/timeout URL would raise and can abort the whole Thor import loop. Also, neither `import_remote` nor `TopicEmbed.import` accepts/forwards `created_at`, and the `PostCreator` call inside `TopicEmbed.import` does not set `created_at`, so the previously supplied thread timestamp is indeed dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — `permalink: "Permalink"` is defined and referenced nowhere, while no key exists for the retrieval-failure state the loading view cannot display.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds several `en.embed.*` keys. In the new views/controllers, only `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, and `embed.imported_from` are referenced (e.g., `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` and `loading.html.erb`). `embed.permalink` is indeed not referenced anywhere in this diff, but an unused locale string by itself is not a verifiable bug/correctness defect. The second part of the finding (“no key exists for the retrieval-failure state the loading view cannot display”) is not grounded in the diff: there is no implemented retrieval-failure state or UI path—`loading.html.erb` always shows `embed.loading` and reloads after 30s, with no branch that would need a missing translation key. Therefore the finding does not identify a real, verifiable problem introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — an unrelated already-shipped migration is edited to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, a drop-and-recreate flag that silently destroys an existing table on replay and traces to nothing in the embed intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it. If this migration is ever applied in an environment where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., partially-initialized DBs, schema drift, or a replay/reset where the table is present), it can silently destroy existing data. This is a real behavioral change introduced by the diff and is unrelated to the embed feature changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:3 — pure churn in an unrelated migration (trailing-whitespace strip plus deletion of the final newline) inflating the diff with changes no requirement asks for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb only removes a trailing whitespace on a blank line and changes the file’s final newline status (now shows "No newline at end of file"). This is unrelated churn, but it is not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change—it's purely formatting/noise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — the diff deletes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and its `Category.where(name: options[:category])` lookup, removing an existing user-facing CLI capability unconnected to embed URL handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` explicitly removes the `:category` CLI option (and the associated `Category.where(name: options[:category])` lookup / `category:` argument to `PostCreator`). The new implementation calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` without any category parameter, so users can no longer choose an import category via `-c/--category`. This is a concrete, user-facing capability regression introduced by the diff (whether intended or not).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — the importer rewrite silently drops the topic's `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` (replies at line 164 keep theirs, so imported replies now predate their own topic) and turns an offline import into a live per-thread HTTP scrape.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor replaces the original topic creation (`PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)`) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which (per TopicEmbed.import_remote) performs `open(url).read` and scrapes the remote page via ruby-readability. This both (1) drops explicitly setting the topic’s `created_at`, meaning the topic will default to “now” instead of the Disqus thread’s timestamp, and (2) changes the importer from using only the Disqus export data to making live HTTP requests per thread. Given the surrounding code still iterates through `t[:posts]` and (per the finding) likely preserves per-reply timestamps, this can plausibly cause replies to have timestamps earlier than their topic. The removal of the topic-level created_at is directly verifiable in the diff; the new live HTTP scrape is directly verifiable via import_remote’s `open(url)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a full RSS/Atom feed import synchronously inside a single-URL retrieval that ignores @embed_url entirely, so one visitor on one unknown embed URL imports the entire feed as a side effect.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `perform_retrieve` checks `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` and then calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` unconditionally. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) parses `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item in the feed. This is synchronous from within the single-URL retrieval path and does not filter based on `@embed_url`, so a retrieval for one missing embed URL can trigger importing the entire configured feed as a side effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` adds a global cook/sanitize bypass to every Post, exposed to every PostCreator caller via lib/post_creator.rb:216, with nothing tying it to embed imports.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:11 — `recurrence { hourly }` plus two new runtime gems (ruby-readability, simple-rss) and three site settings ship an entire RSS/Atom ingestion + scraping subsystem the stated intent never asks for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an embedding feature plus feed polling/import support: a scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` with `recurrence { hourly }`, new site settings under `embedding` (including `feed_polling_*`), and new gems (`simple-rss`, `ruby-readability`) used by `PollFeed`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote`. This is an intentional feature addition shown in the code, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect. The claim that the “stated intent never asks for” this subsystem is not grounded in the diff itself and is therefore not a concrete, reviewable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is a copy-paste leftover unused anywhere in the job.

adjudication.rationale: In the new job file `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, it declares `require_dependency 'email/sender'` but the job implementation only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. Nothing in this diff references `Email::Sender` (or any constant from `email/sender`) from this job, so the require is unused. However, this is an unnecessary/dead dependency rather than a functional correctness bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` re-runs the entire hourly feed import synchronously for one cache-missed embed URL, and the per-URL 60s throttle means N distinct URLs fan out to N concurrent whole-feed polls with no global lock.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline before falling back to HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) fetches and parses the entire configured feed URL and iterates all items each time. The only throttle present in `TopicRetriever` is `retrieved_recently?`, which is keyed by `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (per-embed URL). That means multiple distinct embed URLs can bypass each other’s throttles and each trigger a full-feed poll, potentially concurrently (e.g., multiple `RetrieveTopic` jobs). There is no global lock/throttle around feed polling in this diff, so the finding is a real, diff-verifiable performance/correctness concern (unintended repeated whole-feed work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `rss.items.each` has no per-item rescue and `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the whole batch, silently drops the remaining items, and re-fails identically every hour.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` and performs several operations per item (`i.link`/`i.id` selection, `i.content.scrub`, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import`) without any per-item `rescue`. Any exception raised for a single feed item will abort the entire job execution and prevent remaining items from being processed in that run. Additionally, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means Sidekiq will not retry the failed job instance, so processing resumes only on the next scheduled run (and can fail again if the same problematic item is still present). The only overstatement is "silently"—it will error/likely be logged—but the batch-abort/no-retry behavior is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — the raw URL string is the article's identity with no canonicalization while the feed supplies `i.link`, so any utm/trailing-slash/fragment variant misses the unique index and scrapes a second duplicate topic, permanently splitting the comment thread.

adjudication.rationale: The code uses the exact `embed_url` string as the identity key everywhere (e.g., `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does an exact match, the table has a unique index on `embed_url`, and `TopicRetriever`/`TopicEmbed.import` check/store `embed_url` without normalization). `embed.js` passes `discourseEmbedUrl` verbatim (only URL-encoded) to `/embed/best`. Because there is no canonicalization/normalization (removing UTM params, trailing slashes, fragments, etc.), different URL variants for the same article will not match the existing `topic_embeds.embed_url` and can create separate topics/threads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — replacing the local PostCreator call with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` drops archive `created_at`, deletes the documented -c/--category option, and makes bulk import depend on a live per-thread HTTP scrape with no timeout; a dead source URL silently discards that thread's comments via `if post.present?`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the `:category` option entirely and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id`, so `-c/--category` is no longer supported. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and neither `TopicEmbed.import_remote` nor `TopicEmbed.import` pass through `created_at` or a category, so imported topics will no longer preserve the Disqus thread timestamp or category selection. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` without specifying any open/read timeouts, making the import depend on live HTTP fetches that can hang. Finally, the existing `if post.present?` guard means if the remote import returns nil/fails to create a post, the thread’s comments are skipped (though an actual network exception would likely abort unless handled elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — `Topic.transaction do ... creator.create ... end` makes PostCreator's inner transaction join the outer one, so enqueue_jobs fires while the outer transaction is open (contradicting post_creator.rb:288's own comment) and a TopicEmbed.create! unique violation orphans jobs pointing at rolled-back post ids.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `TopicEmbed.import` wrapping `PostCreator.new(...).create` and `TopicEmbed.create!` inside `Topic.transaction`. It does not show that `PostCreator` uses an “inner transaction”, nor that it enqueues jobs during `create`, nor any referenced “post_creator.rb:288” comment. Without that, the claim that jobs fire while an outer transaction is open (and become orphaned on rollback) is not verifiable from this diff. While there is a potential race around `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` vs the unique index on `embed_url`, that is a different issue than the finding’s specific transaction/job-orphaning assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:79 — `pluck(:topic_id).first` returns a stale id with no existence/visibility check and no FK or dependent: :destroy, so a deleted topic makes TopicView.new raise on every load while topic_retriever.rb:37's exists? bail blocks re-import — permanently unrecoverable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) implemented as `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` and EmbedController#best unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` when that returns a value. There is no existence check that the referenced Topic still exists. Also, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve starts with `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so if a TopicEmbed row remains after the topic/post is deleted (the migration adds no foreign keys/cascade, and TopicEmbed model adds no dependent cleanup), the retriever will stop and never re-import for that URL. This creates a credible stale-record failure mode grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` and `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` have no open/read timeout, no size cap and no circuit breaker on a path driven by unauthenticated inbound requests, so one slow or huge remote host pins workers and materializes an unbounded document in memory.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote fetching via `open-uri` in two places: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). Both read the entire response into memory and do not set explicit open/read timeouts or any maximum size/streaming limit. Additionally, `EmbedController#best` can enqueue `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` based on a request parameter (`embed_url`), which can trigger `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` from an unauthenticated request path (only guarded by referer/host checks), so a slow/large response from the allowed host can tie up job/web workers and allocate unbounded memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — the 30s reload plus `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` forms an unbounded retry loop with no terminal failure state, so an un-importable URL re-enqueues a retrieve (and a full feed poll) once per minute forever.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(... reload(), 30000)`), so the browser will hit `/embed/best` repeatedly and enqueue a new `retrieve_topic` job each time. If the URL can never be imported (e.g., fetch/parse keeps failing), there is no terminal state: the page will keep reloading and jobs will keep getting enqueued indefinitely. While `TopicRetriever` throttles *work* to ~once per 60s per URL via Redis, it does not prevent repeated enqueueing, and `perform_retrieve` can still run forever over time (including `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when enabled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — check-then-insert TOCTOU whose only real guard is the unique index, with no rescue RecordNotUnique/upsert, so the concurrent loser raises out of import instead of converging to the update branch.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters a transaction and calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. There is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, but no locking or rescue around `create!`. Under concurrent imports of the same URL, both callers can observe `embed.blank?` and attempt `create!`; the loser will hit the unique index and raise (e.g., ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique/StatementInvalid) instead of falling back to the update path. This is a real TOCTOU/concurrency correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `post = embed.post` dereferences a belongs_to with no FK and no nil guard, and revise + `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` are not in one transaction, so a crash between them leaves the sha1 stale; update_column also skips updated_at.

adjudication.rationale: The update path in `TopicEmbed.import` is not atomic: when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found, it does `post = embed.post` and then, if the SHA differs, runs `revisor.revise!(...)` and separately `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. There is no surrounding transaction, so a crash/exception after revising but before updating `content_sha1` leaves the row with stale `content_sha1`, causing repeated revisions on subsequent imports/polls. Also, `update_column` bypasses callbacks and does not update `updated_at`, which is a verifiable behavior of Rails and can break timestamp semantics. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url, null: false` is varchar(255) and is the UNIQUE key, fed untrusted external values including the Atom `i.id` fallback, so any URL over 255 chars raises PG::StringDataRightTruncation and kills the whole feed batch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — hard-codes exactly one embedding origin as a bare scalar compared by exact equality with no normalization or setting validation, so a www. prefix, port, or case difference silently 403s every embed request with no diagnostic.

However, it is not “hard-coded” (it uses a site setting), and it does provide a diagnostic by raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess` with a specific message (`'invalid referer host'` / `'embeddable host not set'`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — `feed_key` is defined and never called anywhere; the conditional-GET/change-detection (and only plausible cross-process poll lock) it names is unimplemented, so every poll re-downloads and re-hashes the entire feed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` bypasses the entire sanitizing cook pipeline for remotely-fetched third-party HTML, later emitted verbatim via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, turning any HTML on the embedded site into stored XSS on the forum's origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` entity-decodes attacker-influenced feed bodies and hands them to TopicEmbed.import with zero sanitization, so a feed item containing `<script>` becomes a live `<script>` in a raw_html post.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `"#{url}"` interpolates the unvalidated, unescaped source URL into a single-quoted attribute after Readability's whitelist runs, so a URL containing `'` injects an event handler into content rendered raw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` makes a spoofable header the sole authorization gate, so any unauthenticated curl with a forged Referer drives the server-side fetch + topic-creation primitive behind it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — `retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` throttles per exact URL string, so appending a unique query param bypasses the 60s limiter entirely, allowing unbounded outbound fetches, Redis key growth, and auto-created public topics (spam + resource exhaustion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open-uri follows HTTP redirects without re-applying the embeddable_host check (which itself ignores scheme, port, and userinfo), so one open redirect pivots the fetch to 169.254.169.254 or any internal service and publishes the response as a public post (SSRF).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` added to an already-shipped unrelated migration emits DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, so any replay silently destroys the populated ranking table and indexes, while already-migrated deployments never re-run it and diverge from fresh installs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` converts a loud "table already exists" failure into silent destruction of the only (non-rebuildable) record of the external-URL↔topic mapping, so one replay makes every embedded page create a duplicate topic.

The finding’s scenario (table already exists with non-rebuildable data, migration runs again, mapping destroyed leading to duplicates) is not verifiable from this diff and requires an atypical state (preexisting `topic_embeds` table or re-running the same migration). adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — `topic_id`/`post_id` NOT NULL get no FK, no index, and no dependent: cleanup; with Trashable hiding soft-deleted posts, a moderator deletion orphans the row → `PostRevisor.new(nil)` NoMethodError escapes rss.items.each and (retry: false) permanently aborts the hourly poll for every later item.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on the largest table inside the default DDL transaction forces a full rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on 2013-era PG, locking all reads/writes; the sibling migration already demonstrates the disable_ddl_transaction! + batched-backfill pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255), so a >255-char feed/permalink URL raises inside Topic.transaction, rolling back the just-created topic and post and killing the poll job; :text or an explicit limit is required.

In TopicEmbed.import, `embed_url: url` is inserted inside a `Topic.transaction` via `TopicEmbed.create!`. If a feed/permalink URL exceeds 255 chars, many DBs (e.g., Postgres) will raise on insert (or MySQL may truncate/raise depending on SQL mode), causing the transaction to roll back and the job to error (PollFeed has no rescue and is configured `sidekiq_options retry: false`). adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:11 — `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true` makes a raw un-normalized externally-supplied URL the natural key, so scheme/slash/utm variants create duplicate topics and any later canonicalization backfill collides with this index requiring a manual lossy dedupe with no reversible path.

In the diff, all lookups and writes use the raw externally supplied URL value as-is (e.g., `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`, and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does an exact match). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:456 — the `# == Schema Information` annotation is the only checked-in schema record in this tree (no db/schema.rb) and was not regenerated for the new cook_method column, so the committed schema record and the migration disagree.
